doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: Studying with Konitz and Harold Danko
summary: He did not quit college for music; he left Konitz when the lessons ran their course and studied piano and chord voicing for two years with Harold Danko, a fellow Youngstown native.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Were you ever tempted at that time to call up Mom and Dad and say, “Listen, I’m not going to major anymore in what I’m doing, I have to be a musician.”

No. I didn’t have the guts. Plus I was, you know, this was my excuse for being in New York. So I mean I was studying with Konitz for a couple of years and then I started studying for a couple of years with Harold Danko, who by the way is also from Youngstown, Ohio, although I used to play outdoor concerts with his older brothers who were both saxophone players. We would play concert band gigs in Youngstown. And I didn’t meet Harold until 1973 when we were both in New York. He had just gotten off Woody Herman’s band. So I got his number and I called him and we hooked up and had an instant friendship. We’re really good friends ‘til this day. And I started studying with him and it was perfect because I had stopped studying with Lee because basically, without saying so I think Lee had come to the point where we couldn’t, there was nothing more he could teach me or felt that he could teach me. And I felt like I still had so much to learn. And luckily I met Harold just at that moment and it was perfect because I desperately needed some basic piano chops, you know, how to voice chords, 2-5-1s and things like that. And Harold was perfect because he’s a great teacher. And he would go anywhere you wanted to go. He had no preconceived notions of anything. So he was the perfect teacher for me that I needed at precisely that moment. So I studied with him for two years and it was great.
